column3: The Hebrew uses plural sons for Uzzi, though only Izrahiah follows; BSB uses singular son.
The Hebrew explicitly names sons rather than the broader children and includes their fathers’ house.
The Hebrew names Benjamin directly without a separate sons.
The Hebrew uses plural sons for Jediael, though only Bilhan follows; BSB uses singular son.
The Hebrew twice uses an active birth verb with a feminine subject; BSB recasts the relationships as descent through a concubine.
The Hebrew calls him the second without a separate descendant and says he had daughters without only.
The Hebrew uses plural sons for Ulam, though only Bedan follows; BSB uses singular son.
The Hebrew makes the men of Gath active killing agents; BSB uses passive were killed. It says take their livestock without explicitly saying steal.
The Hebrew names his brothers; BSB uses relatives.
The Hebrew says he went in to his wife without again; BSB says again he slept with her.
The Hebrew does not repeat his son after Resheph; BSB supplies it.
The Hebrew retains the image of daughters for the dependent settlements; BSB uses villages.
The Hebrew repeats daughters with each town; BSB combines them as their villages.
